name: time-wheel
title: Time Wheel
description: Wheels for a time of day: rows tilt away like a drum, each wheel snaps row by row with a tick.

perf.budget: Native scroll views; each row reads its wheel's scroll offset in one animated style. Nothing runs at rest.

measurements.notes: Janky frames come from the native fling and snap of the scroll views; rows stay at 17 ms median.

a11y.reducedMotion: Rows stay flat and changes from outside jump instead of scrolling.
a11y.screenReader: Each wheel is an adjustable element named after its part of the time, with the shown value.

meta.guide:
## Usage

```tsx
import { TimeWheel } from '@/components/kinetik/time-wheel';

<TimeWheel
  accessibilityLabel="Alarm"
  value={time} // { hours: 7, minutes: 30 }
  onChange={setTime}
  minuteStep={5}
/>;
```

## When to use

- Setting a time of day: an alarm, a reminder, opening hours, a delivery window.
- Places where a thumb is quicker than typing digits.

## When not to use

- Durations or countdown lengths beyond 24 hours. Use Roll Stepper or a number field.
- Picking a date. Use Month Calendar.

## Notes

- `value.hours` is always 0–23, also with `hourCycle="12h"`, which adds an AM/PM wheel.
- Each wheel snaps row by row and ticks as rows pass the middle; the value is set when the wheel comes to rest.
- Every wheel is an adjustable element: screen readers can swipe up and down to step it.
- With reduced motion rows stay flat (no tilt) and programmatic changes jump instead of scrolling.

docs: Prefer `npx kinetik-ui add time-wheel`: it installs dependencies with expo install, so versions match your Expo SDK.
